title: Human Inability
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Human inability means that sinners cannot rescue themselves, make themselves righteous, or come to God apart from His grace. Sin leaves humanity morally unable to save itself, though still responsible before God.
summary: Human inability means that sinners cannot rescue themselves, make themselves righteous, or come to God apart from His grace. Sin leaves humanity morally unable to save itself, though still responsible before God.
christFocus: Jesus Christ saves those who cannot save themselves. The Father draws sinners to the Son, and the Spirit gives life so helpless people truly come to Christ by grace.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Human inability does not mean people are machines or that they never make choices. It means fallen sinners are unable to overcome their own corruption, satisfy God’s righteousness, or come to Christ apart from grace.

Scripture describes sinners as dead in trespasses, hostile to God, unable to submit to His law, and unable to receive spiritual things rightly. The problem is moral and spiritual, not merely informational.

This inability does not remove responsibility. Sinners still choose sin willingly and are accountable before God. Inability shows the depth of bondage, not innocence.

The hope of the Gospel is that God saves the unable. He makes the dead alive, draws sinners to Christ, and grants mercy not because people first made themselves worthy, but because He is gracious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Human inability destroys self-salvation. People cannot climb to God through religion, willpower, morality, recovery progress, or sincerity. They need saving grace from beginning to end.

This doctrine also gives hope to hard cases. No person is beyond God because they lack ability. Salvation depends on the mercy and power of God, not on the sinner’s strength.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Stop trusting yourself as your own rescuer. Confess your inability and ask God for mercy, faith, repentance, and life in Christ. When praying for others, do not despair over their hardness; ask God to do what only He can do.
